Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class X11DamageExt

java.lang.Object
gnu.x11.extension.Extension
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.X11DamageExt
All Implemented Interfaces:
gnu.x11.extension.EventFactory
public class X11DamageExt extends gnu.x11.extension.Extension implements gnu.x11.extension.EventFactory
Pure-Java Escher binding for the X Damage extension (version 1.1).

Damage reports which regions of a drawable have changed since the last time the client acknowledged them. Combined with Composite (which redirects a window's rendering into an offscreen pixmap), Damage is how a compositor knows when to re-read a window's contents. lg3d uses it to trigger texture re-uploads for NativeWindow3D quads only when the underlying X11 app actually repaints, instead of polling every frame.

Protocol reference: Damage Extension Protocol, Version 1.1.

Usage in lg3d

  1. create(int, gnu.x11.Drawable, int) a Damage object on the window's NameWindowPixmap with REPORT_LEVEL_NON_EMPTY.
  2. Listen for X11DamageExt.NotifyEvent on the X event loop.
  3. On each event, read the damaged region from the pixmap (via XShm or GetImage), then call subtract(int, int, int) with repair=None to acknowledge and reset the damage.
  4. destroy(int) when the window is unmapped or the compositor shuts down.

    • REPORT_LEVEL_NON_EMPTY

      public static final int REPORT_LEVEL_NON_EMPTY
      Reports a single event whenever the damage becomes non-empty (i.e. transitions from clean to dirty). The area field covers the entire drawable. This is the level lg3d uses: one notification per repaint burst, then the compositor reads the full window (or the damaged region from the geometry fields).
      See Also:

      public X11DamageExt(gnu.x11.Display display) throws gnu.x11.extension.NotFoundException

    • subtract

      public void subtract(int damage, int repair, int parts)
      Acknowledges (subtracts) damage. Passing repair=0 (None) and parts=0 (None) subtracts ALL accumulated damage, resetting the Damage object to the empty state. This is the standard "ack" call a compositor makes after reading the damaged pixels.
      Parameters:
      damage - the damage object to acknowledge
      repair - an XFixes region to subtract, or 0 for None (subtract all)
      parts - an XFixes region that receives the subtracted area, or 0

    • subtract

      public void subtract(int damage)
      Convenience: acknowledge all damage (repair=None, parts=None).

    • add

      public void add(gnu.x11.Drawable drawable, int region)
      Manually adds damage to a drawable. This is used by clients that draw directly to a redirected window's pixmap and need to inform the compositor. lg3d does not normally call this.
      Parameters:
      drawable - the drawable to mark as damaged
      region - an XFixes region describing the damaged area
